title: Mixed conditionals
instructions: Put the verb in brackets into the correct form. Think: which time does each clause refer to?

items.q: If I ______ (not / miss) the train this morning, I wouldn't be so stressed now.
If she ______ (be) more organised in general, she would have finished the report on time.
If we had invested in that company ten years ago, we ______ (be) rich now.
items.why: Past condition -> present result: would + infinitive.

items.q: If he ______ (speak) better English in general, he would have got the job last month.
I ______ (not / ask) you for help yesterday if I didn't trust you.
items.why: Present situation (I trust you) -> past result (yesterday).

items.q: If the government had acted sooner, the crisis ______ (not / be) so severe today.
You ______ (not / feel) so tired now if you had gone to bed earlier.
If I ______ (know) him better (I hardly know him now), I would have invited him to the wedding last month.
items.why: 'I don't know him well' is a present state -> past result.

title: Inverted conditionals and 'but for'
instructions: Complete the second sentence so it means the same as the first. Write only the missing words.

items.q:
If I had known about the problem, I would have helped.
______ about the problem, I would have helped.

If you need any further information, please contact us.
______ any further information, please contact us.

If the president resigned, there would be an election.
______ resign, there would be an election.

If it hadn't been for your help, I would have failed.
______ your help, I would have failed.
items.why: Negative inversion keeps 'not' after the subject: Had it NOT been for... (never *Hadn't it been*).

items.q:
If they had not cancelled the flight, we would be in Rome now.
______ the flight, we would be in Rome now.

If it weren't for the rain, we could eat outside.
______ the rain, we could eat outside.
Take an umbrella ___ it rains later.
items.why: Precaution = in case. (Take it now because it might rain.)

items.q: You can borrow my car ___ you bring it back by six.
I won't go to the party ___ you come with me.
___ you won the lottery, what would you do first?
___ the storm, we would have arrived on time.
Leave now; ___, you'll miss the bus.
I'm going to the concert ___ you like it or not.
___ she apologised, I still wouldn't forgive her.

title: Wishes and unreal past
instructions: Put the verb in brackets into the correct form.

items.q: I wish I ______ (have) more free time - I'm exhausted.
She wishes she ______ (not / sell) her old flat; prices have doubled since.
I wish my neighbours ______ (stop) playing loud music every night.
items.why: wish + would = annoying habit of someone else that you want to change.

items.q: If only I ______ (listen) to your advice last year!
It's high time the government ______ (do) something about housing.
I'd rather you ______ (not / tell) anyone about this yet.
He talks as if he ______ (be) the boss, but he's just an intern.
I'd rather ______ (stay) at home tonight, if you don't mind.
Come on, it's time ______ (leave); the taxi's waiting.
I wish I ______ (can) speak Japanese.

title: Negative inversion
instructions: Complete the second sentence so it means the same as the first. Write only the missing words.

items.q:
I have never seen such a beautiful sunset.
Never ______ such a beautiful sunset.

As soon as I arrived, the phone rang.
No sooner ______ than the phone rang.

He didn't realise the danger he was in.
Little ______ the danger he was in.

You must not open this door under any circumstances.
Under no circumstances ______ this door.

She not only wrote the script, but she also directed the film.
Not only ______ the script, but she also directed the film.

I only understood the problem after reading the report.
Only after reading the report ______ the problem.
items.why: With 'Only after/when/by', the inversion happens in the MAIN clause.

items.q:
We didn't find out the truth until years later.
Not until years later ______ the truth.

The noise was so loud that we couldn't sleep.
So ______ that we couldn't sleep.

The demand was so high that tickets sold out in minutes.
Such ______ that tickets sold out in minutes.

We had hardly sat down when the lights went out.
Hardly ______ down when the lights went out.

People rarely get a second chance like this.
Rarely ______ a second chance like this.

You can't find better coffee anywhere in the city.
Nowhere in the city ______ better coffee.

title: Cleft sentences
instructions: Complete the second sentence so it means the same as the first. Write only the missing words.

items.q:
I need a long holiday.
What ______ a long holiday.

Her attitude annoys me, not her work.
It's ______ annoys me, not her work.

I only want some peace and quiet.
All ______ some peace and quiet.

He moved back home because he lost his job.
The reason ______ that he lost his job.
a: why he moved back home was

items.q:
We didn't discover the error until Friday.
It ______ Friday that we discovered the error.

She called the police.
What she ______ call the police.

The manager made the final decision.
It ______ made the final decision.

I love the way she explains things.
What ______ the way she explains things.

Something strange happened: the lights went off.
What ______ that the lights went off.

I met my wife in Lisbon.
Lisbon ______ I met my wife.
Never I have seen such chaos.
a: Never have I seen such chaos.
I have never seen such chaos.

items.q: If I would have known, I would have come.
a: If I had known, I would have come.
Had I known, I would have come.

items.q: I wish I would be taller.
Only when he left I realised my mistake.
a: Only when he left did I realise my mistake.
Only when he left did I realize my mistake.

items.q: What I need it is more time.
a: What I need is more time.

items.q: It's time we go home.
Hardly had we arrived than it started to rain.
a: Hardly had we arrived when it started to rain.
Hardly had we arrived before it started to rain.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.

items.q: Had I not been so tired, I would go out last night.
a: Had I not been so tired, I would have gone out last night.

items.q: Hadn't it been for you, we would have lost.
a: Had it not been for you, we would have lost.

items.q: Call me in case you need anything, and I'll come.
a: Call me if you need anything, and I'll come.
Call me if you need anything and I'll come.
